answer: Neighborhood-Density Admission. Each agent maintains a routing beacon listing its live neighbors. Join requests are admitted only if the applicant's neighbor set overlaps ≥40% with the existing graph's local density (measured over a sliding window). A sybil cluster appears hollow: internally dense but sparsely linked to honest nodes, so overlapping frontiers reject it. The prism is a sampling rule: verifiers request random second-hop witnesses, refracting the claimed neighborhood into checkable paths.
